coding.side_b_parties: Cellco Partnership, dba Verizon Wireless (accused infringer, defendant-appellee)

issues.description: Appellate jurisdiction: Verizon argued the Federal Circuit lacked jurisdiction because the action turns on nonpatent issues; the court held the appeal arises under federal patent law because the independent action is in substance a challenge to a §285 fee award.
issues.quote: We conclude that we have appellate jurisdiction over Traxcell’s case because it arises under federal patent law.

issues.description: Subject-matter jurisdiction of the Western District of Texas over an independent action under Rule 60(d)(1) to void a judgment of the Eastern District of Texas and an affirmed fee award; the court held the district court lacked jurisdiction under Beggerly and because it could not set aside an affirmed judgment.
issues.quote: However, we conclude the district court did not have jurisdiction over Traxcell’s independent action. Accordingly, we vacate the district court’s judgment and remand with instructions to dismiss the case for want of jurisdiction.

coding.author: Dyk
coding.notes: Unanimous panel as far as the opinion shows; no separate opinions noted. The Federal Circuit raised district-court jurisdiction sua sponte, and the court did not reach the merits of the mandate-rule or §285 arguments.

coding.case_type: Federal employment (MSPB, arbitrator, OCWR, back-pay claims)

issues.description: Trial and case management: the administrative judge's exclusion of agency witness Ferguson based on the parties' stipulated facts was not an abuse of discretion.
issues.quote: The administrative judge did not abuse his discretion.

issues.description: Due process: employee's claim that the stipulation was improperly characterized without notice, and that the witness exclusion caused harmful error, was rejected.
issues.quote: We find that Mr. Butlak fails to raise an issue of due process because the administrative judge did not rely upon any new information of which Mr. Butlak was entitled to receive notice.

issues.description: Penalty reasonableness: removal sustained as reasonable, including upholding the Giglio-impairment aggravating factor and rejecting the comparator (consistency) argument.
issues.quote: We therefore decline to disturb the administrative judge’s aggravation finding on this ground.

coding.author: Hughes
coding.notes: Nonprecedential disposition affirming MSPB removal for lack of candor and conduct unbecoming. Charges were sustained and not challenged on appeal, so no adverse-action merits issue (E01) was coded. No dissent.

coding.side_b_parties: VF Outdoor, LLC; Columbia Sportswear Company

issues.description: Indefiniteness under §112(b) of the MVTR limitation in asserted claims 1, 38 and 39 of the '287 patent; the court held the claims indefinite and invalid, and rejected Cocona's argument that the district court applied the wrong legal standard.
issues.quote: Applying that standard here, we reach the same conclusion as the district court: the asserted claims are indefinite.

coding.author: Stark
coding.notes: Affirmance of district court judgment of invalidity for indefiniteness. Court found clear and convincing evidence of indefiniteness and no clear error in extrinsic findings. No separate dissent or concurrence noted.

issues.description: Claim construction of 'manifold': the district court erred by declining to construe the disputed term, so the summary judgment of noninfringement is vacated and remanded for construction and further analysis, which favors the patent owner.
issues.quote: We disagree that construing “manifold” was unnecessary.

issues.description: Cartessa argued Edge waived or forfeited its preferred construction of 'manifold' by not raising it during claim construction; the court rejected the waiver/forfeiture argument, so the argument was preserved.
issues.quote: We see no waiver or forfeiture under the circumstances here.

issues.description: Anticipation of claim 1 by Shadduck (the selectable-container element): no reasonable jury could find by clear and convincing evidence that Shadduck anticipates, so the summary judgment of no invalidity is affirmed.
issues.quote: We conclude that no reasonable jury could find by clear and convincing evidence that Shadduck discloses claim 1’s selectable element, and we therefore affirm the district court’s summary judgment of no invalidity.

coding.author: PROST
coding.notes: Nonprecedential disposition. Vacated in part and affirmed in part; costs to Edge. No separate opinions or dissents are reflected in the text. The court did not reach Cartessa's alternative grounds for affirmance (fluid communication, direct infringement), so those are not coded. The noninfringement ruling is coded as a claim construction remand under P11 rather than a P12 merits ruling.
